newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bomb defense will not get taped phone calls.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bomb defense will not get taped phone calls.

text.p: Prison recordings of telephone conversations between a husband and wife who are expected to be key prosecution witnesses in the Oklahoma City bombing case will not be turned over to the defence, a judge ruled Wednesday.
Lawyers for defendant Timothy McVeigh had subpoenad a copy of the recordings of conversations between Michael Fortier and his wife, Lori.

Michael Fortier of Kingman, Arizona, is in prison awaiting sentencing. He has pleaded guilty to knowing about the bombing before the April 1995 attack on the Alfred P. Murrah federal building that claimed the lives of 168 people.
Lori Fortier has been granted immunity. Both are expected to testify at McVeigh's trial, which begins March 31.

U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch granted Fortier's and Justice Department prosecutors' requests to quash the subpoena, noting that the prison recordings are made only as a security measure and to release them would subvert that purpose.
McVeighs' lawyers had claimed that the Fortiers have been collaborating on their testimony for the trial.
